sq.q: \(\text{Given half-range sine series } f(x) = \sum b_n \sin nx \text{ with } b_n = \frac{2}{n}, \text{ find RMS value.}\)
\(\text{Explain why harmonic analysis gives approximate Fourier coefficients.}\)
answer: \(\text{Uses numerical integration (trapezoidal rule) instead of exact integrals}\)
\(\text{Approximation error depends on number of data points}\)
\(\text{More points give better approximation to integrals}\)

Step Marks Period 4 ⇒ \(l=2\) (1) \(a_0=\frac{1}{2}\int_{-2}^2 f(x)dx=\frac{1}{2}\left[\int_{-2}^0 2\,dx+\int_0^2 x\,dx\right]=\frac{3}{2}\) (3) \(a_n=\frac{1}{2}\int_{-2}^2 f(x)\cos\frac{n\pi x}{2}dx=\frac{1}{2}\left[2\int_{-2}^0 \cos\frac{n\pi x}{2}dx+\int_0^2 x\cos\frac{n\pi x}{2}dx\right]=-\frac{4}{n^2\pi^2}[1-(-1)^n]\) (4) \(b_n=\frac{1}{2}\int_{-2}^2 f(x)\sin\frac{n\pi x}{2}dx=\frac{1}{2}\left[2\int_{-2}^0 \sin\frac{n\pi x}{2}dx+\int_0^2 x\sin\frac{n\pi x}{2}dx\right]=-\frac{2}{n\pi}[1+2(-1)^n]\) (4) Thus, \(f(x)=\frac{3}{4}-\frac{4}{\pi^2}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1-(-1)^n}{n^2}\cos\frac{n\pi x}{2}-\frac{2}{\pi}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1+2(-1)^n}{n}\sin\frac{n\pi x}{2}\) (2) Put \(x=1\) for (i) and \(x=0\) for (ii) (1)
